# Operations: documents, moves, stock and runs

Owned by the **operations** module ([architecture.md](architecture.md) §2). This is the
successor to ATI's MTR ledger (`mtr_reg`) and to the order, receiving, shipping and shop tools
built around it.

## 1. Purpose and model

All material movement is recorded as **moves** of a quantity of one part between two
**locations**. Moves are generated by **documents**: quotes, orders, POs, runs, transfers,
adjustments and counts. Stock on hand, availability and projections are maintained summaries
of the moves. This is ATI's design (one ledger, with planning as a filter over statuses),
with three changes ([../legacy/Findings.md](../legacy/Findings.md) §5):

1. **Documents are separate from moves.** A quote line is not a move. In ATI, 61% of
   `mtr_reg` was quote lines that never moved anything.
2. **Done moves are immutable.** They are corrected by reversing moves.
3. **Balances are maintained,** not summed from history on every read. **Demand is registered
   at commit**, and allocating specific stock is an optional extra step. **Locations are
   separate from accounts.**

## 2. Locations

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| id, code, name | e.g. `MAIN`, `MAIN/A-03`, `SHOP-ELEC` |
| kind | see below |
| parent | Hierarchy (site → room → bin). Balances roll up |
| party | For `vendor`, `customer` and `shop` locations: the party in the parties module |
| valuation | The valuation class used for postings (§14) |
| planning_group | The set of stock locations that planning treats as one pool (default: the site) |
| active | |

| Kind | What it is | Valuation (default) |
|---|---|---|
| `stock` | Where stocked parts are kept | Inventory (optionally raw or finished) |
| `wip` | A production area, in-house shop or outside shop, holding material issued to runs | WIP |
| `job` | A customer installation or job site, for material sent to a project before it is billed | Jobs in process |
| `transit` | Goods shipped but not yet received between our locations | Inventory in transit |
| `vendor` | External source (one per vendor, or one generic) | none: crossing it posts a receipt |
| `customer` | External destination | none: crossing it posts COGS |
| `scrap` | Scrapped material | none: scrap expense |
| `adjust` | The counterpart of count and adjustment moves | none: inventory variance |

ATI: projects served as locations, cost centers and accounts. Here a location is only a place.
Accounting meaning comes from its `valuation` class, which maps to Bonum accounts, with the
document as a Bonum tag (WIP by run or PO, jobs by customer order).

## 3. Documents

Every document has a header (type, number, party, dates, status, owner, notes) and lines.

| Type | Purpose | Generates moves |
|---|---|---|
| `quote` | Sales proposal, with a win probability | **No.** Contributes *soft demand* to planning only (§13) |
| `order` | Customer order (DIY kit, equipment, or installation) | On commit: stock → customer (or → job) |
| `po` | Purchase order to a vendor for whole parts | On commit: vendor → stock |
| `run` | Production batch, in-house or at an outside shop (§9) | On commit: components stock → wip (demand on inventory); output wip → stock (supply) |
| `transfer` | Move between our locations | On commit |
| `adjust` | Correction, scrap, or reclassification of material (§12) | On post |
| `count` | Physical count | On post: differences against `adjust` |

### Document status

```
draft ──commit──► committed ──(all lines closed)──► closed
  │                  │
  └──void            └──void (only lines with nothing done)
```

* **draft:** editable. No planned moves (ATI `work`). A draft quote can be *converted*
  into an order, and the order keeps a link to the quote.
* **committed:** the lines generate **planned** moves (ATI `open`). Header edits are limited.
  Line changes go through amendments, which adjust the planned moves.
* **closed:** every line is fully done or cancelled. The document is immutable.
* **void:** cancelled before anything was done. Its planned moves become void.

### Document line
part number (with version or version policy), quantity, unit price, due date, from/to
locations (with defaults from the header), status, and `parent_line` for lines generated from
a package or a run explosion (§8). A line's **remaining quantity** is its quantity minus done
and cancelled quantities.

## 4. Moves

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| id | |
| doc_line | The document line that generated it (required) |
| part, ver | Part number and version. `0` if unknown or not tracked ([product.md](product.md) §3) |
| lot | A run ID, a vendor lot, or none. Required if the part's tracking is `run` or `serial` |
| serial | For serial-tracked parts. One move per serial, or a serial range record |
| qty | > 0, exact, in the part's unit ([architecture.md](architecture.md) §7) |
| from, to | Locations. Must differ |
| state | `planned` → `done` or `void` |
| planned_date | When it is expected (drives planning) |
| done_at, done_by | When and by whom it was executed |
| unit_cost | Set when it becomes done (§14) |
| reverses | For a reversing move: the move it reverses |

**Invariants**
* A `done` move is immutable. A correction is a new move in the opposite direction with
  `reverses` set, and a reason.
* **Partial execution splits the move:** executing 30 of a planned 50 produces a done move of
  30 and leaves a planned move of 20, linked as its successor. This is ATI's automatic
  back-order.
* A move's quantity never exceeds its document line's remaining quantity.
* For `serial` parts, done moves into a stock location must carry serials. A serial can be
  on hand in only one location at a time.
* Stock can't go negative in a `stock` location, unless the location allows it (default:
  warn, don't block, because data entry order in the real world isn't perfect).

## 5. Lots, runs and serials

* **Lot = run** for parts built in-house or by a shop: the run ID (`R27-014`) is the lot.
  Purchased parts MAY carry a vendor lot.
* **Serial = run ID + sequence** (`R27-014-007`), allocated at completion (Q5). It can
  be opaque to the customer. A product label MAY show a shorter form.
* A serial's history (its run, the run's version and minor revision, QC results, shipment,
  returns) is a query over moves and run records.

## 6. Balances, demand and allocation

**Balance:** a maintained row per (part, version, location, lot), holding `on_hand`. It is
updated in the same transaction that makes a move done. It is a Quereus maintained or
materialized table, never a scan of the moves on read.

**Demand is registered when a document is committed, not when material is picked.** Committing
an order or a run creates its planned outgoing moves at once. A run's component moves
(stock → wip) are therefore demand on inventory from the moment the run exists, and so is each
order line's shipment move. While a purchasing round is open, its awarded component lines
already count as demand ([purchasing.md](purchasing.md) §4), as ATI's `wt` MTRs did. Every
planning figure (§13), including **coverage**, which tells whether each outstanding order and
run can be satisfied, comes from these planned moves.

**Allocation** is an optional, *additional* step: tying a planned outgoing move to **specific**
on-hand stock. Fields: the move, a balance row (part, version, location, lot), and a quantity.
Use it when:
* a demand must take a particular lot or serial (traceability, a matched set);
* a demand must be protected from others that fall due earlier, overriding the default
  due-date priority in coverage (§13);
* stock is physically set aside (picked or staged).

Rules:
* **Invariant:** allocated ≤ on hand per balance row.
* Executing the move consumes its allocation.
* Without an allocation, a demand is still fully counted. It just isn't tied to particular
  units, and coverage assigns stock by due date.

`free = on_hand − allocated`, per balance row and rolled up.

## 7. Instantiating engine results

When an engine result becomes document lines (a package on an order, a run's components):
* each leaf's extended quantity is **rounded up to the component unit's scale** (default; a
  family MAY specify `round: nearest`). This applies per generated line, not per node;
* identical leaf parts under the same parent line are summed into one line;
* the result's `hash`, `engine_version` and family-version map are stored on the parent line.
  The full result MAY be stored compressed for audit;
* a leaf with status `missing_part` blocks commit, until the configuration is approved as a
  part or the parent's parameters change.

## 8. Order lines, packages and re-explosion

* An order line for a **part** generates one planned outgoing move on commit.
* An order line for a **package** (or for a part whose family has
  `explode_default = to_part`) is exploded with depth `to_part`. The engine result becomes
  **generated child lines** (`parent_line` set), one per resulting part, and their planned
  moves. The parent line holds the package, its parameters, the version used and its price.
  It generates no moves itself.
* Versions are taken as current at instantiation and recorded (Q19). Later releases do
  not change the order.

**Re-explosion** is **manual**, limited to the lines the user selects (Q30):
1. Re-run the engine for each selected parent line, with current versions (or a chosen
   version).
2. Show a **diff** against the existing generated lines: added, removed, quantity changed, or
   unchanged.
3. Each change is **applicable** only if the affected child line has nothing done, nothing
   allocated, and is not awarded in an open purchasing round. Other changes are **flagged** and
   listed for a person to resolve (for example "already picked 4 of 6").
4. On confirmation, apply the applicable changes as amendments (adjust or void planned moves,
   add new lines), and record a re-explosion event with the old and new hashes.

ATI had no clean way to do this, because packages were exploded straight into MTRs with no
parent record.

## 9. Runs (work orders)

A run builds a quantity of one part to a pinned definition.

| Field | Meaning |
|---|---|
| run_id | Human ID, also the lot (`R27-014`) |
| part, ver | What is built, at which version |
| qty | Planned quantity |
| shop | A `wip` location: an in-house shop, or an outside shop's location |
| source | The purchasing round award that created it, or manual |
| po_line | For outside shops: the PO line that pays for the labor ([purchasing.md](purchasing.md)) |
| bom | A one-level engine result (stamped with its hash), instantiated as component lines |
| notes_rev | The minor revision of notes and QC pinned when the run is released |
| status | `planned` (committed) → `released` → `in_progress` → `completed` or `closed`; or `void` |

* **Component lines:** planned moves stock → shop, one per component (ATI `wm`/`wt`), created
  when the run is **committed**, which is normally when a round makes it. From that moment they
  are demand on inventory (§6). Release only hands the run to the floor.
  Issuing executes them. **Backflush** (ATI `bf`) MAY be set per component: the issue
  executes automatically at completion, for the quantity actually consumed.
* **Output line:** a planned move shop → stock for the run quantity. A partial completion
  splits it (§4).
* **Release** pins `notes_rev` and produces the **traveler**: engine `traveler()` + notes as
  of `notes_rev`, by process step. If notes change during the run, the run keeps its pinned
  revision unless a lead re-pins it, which is recorded.
* **QC results** per process step: run, step, criterion, unit serial (or run-level), measured
  value or pass/fail, inspector, time. A failing result MAY hold the unit (a move to a
  quarantine location) until it is dispositioned (rework, scrap, accept with deviation).
* **Close** after completion: the remaining component moves are voided or returned, the run
  cost is computed (§14), and the run record becomes immutable.

## 10. Receiving

* Receive against **PO lines**. Executing the planned move vendor → stock, partially if need
  be, sets `unit_cost` = PO unit price (converted from purchase packs, if the bid had a pack
  size: [purchasing.md](purchasing.md) §3).
* Over-receipt beyond a tolerance (default 0%) needs the `buyer` role.
* Receipts post `receipt` (§14). AP reads receipts to match vendor invoices
  ([architecture.md](architecture.md) §5–6).
* Receipts from an outside shop's run (the output move shop → stock) are handled the same way
  from the receiver's point of view.

## 11. Shipping

* Pick (optionally allocating), pack and ship against order lines. Executing the planned move
  stock → customer (or → job) posts `shipment`.
* Shipments to a `job` location post nothing until the job is billed. Then a move job →
  customer posts `shipment`. That is how complete installations accumulate cost (JIP) before
  revenue.
* Returns are reversing moves with a reason, either back to stock or to quarantine.

## 12. Transfers, adjustments, counts and reclassification

* **Transfer:** between our locations. It posts only if the valuation class changes.
* **Adjust:** for found or lost stock, or scrap. The counterpart is `adjust` or `scrap`.
  A reason code is required.
* **Count:** record counted quantities per balance row, then post the differences as
  adjustments. ATI's `docount` (count request) flag lives in the part's stock policy.
* **Reclassify / transform:** one `adjust` document with consuming lines (part X →
  `adjust`) and producing lines (`adjust` → part Y). Used for remnants, rebundling and
  repacking (ATI used a loose pair of MTRs for this). The value moves from X to Y. Any
  difference goes to variance.

## 13. Planning views

Per part, per **planning group**, and per **version chain** (consecutive versions that are
interchangeable are pooled: [product.md](product.md) §6):

| Figure | Definition |
|---|---|
| on_hand | Σ balances |
| allocated | Σ allocations |
| free | on_hand − allocated |
| open_in | Σ planned incoming moves (POs, run outputs, transfers in) |
| open_out | Σ planned outgoing moves (orders, run components, transfers out) |
| projected | on_hand + open_in − open_out |
| soft_demand | Σ quote line quantity × win probability (ATI `projb`), shown separately and never netted automatically |
| drop_dead | The first date on which projected stock, stepped through planned moves by date, falls below 0 (or below `min_level`, configurable) |
| shortage | max(0, min_level − projected), or the negative projected amount at drop_dead |
| avg_monthly_use | Done outgoing moves to customer, wip and job over the trailing 12 months ÷ 12 |
| months_supply | projected ÷ avg_monthly_use |
| urgency | drop_dead − today − expected lead time (best active bid or run history). Negative means late already. Successor to ATI's "stress" |

**Coverage** answers "do we have enough for every outstanding order and run?" for each part:
1. Take every planned outgoing move: run components, order lines, transfers.
2. Satisfy allocated moves first, from their allocations.
3. Then walk the rest **by due date** (ties by document priority, then age), drawing first on
   free on-hand stock and then on planned incoming moves due on or before the demand's date.
4. Each demand gets a status:
   * `covered` (by stock);
   * `covered_late` or `covered_by_supply` (by which PO or run, and when);
   * `short` (by how much).
5. Runs roll this up across their component lines into **"clear to build"** (all covered by
   stock), **"clear by date"** (covered by supply in time) or **"blocked"** (some component
   short), naming the shortest components.

Coverage is computed and not stored, like ATI's drop-dead walk. It never moves or ties up
stock. The way to *fix* a priority is an allocation (§6).

Plus a **time-phased** view: projected stock in date buckets (week or month) for MRP-style
reading. These are maintained views, or computed incrementally from planned moves, not
computed by scanning the moves on read ([architecture.md](architecture.md) §12).

The **shortage list**, the parts whose urgency or shortage calls for action, is the input to
a purchasing round ([purchasing.md](purchasing.md)).

## 14. Costing and postings

**Valuation:** FIFO cost layers per (part, valuation class), consistent with Bonum's default
costing method. **Open:** support moving average if Bonum's entity setting says so.

* **Receipt:** creates a layer at the PO unit price. When AP matches the invoice, a price
  difference adjusts the layer if that stock is still on hand. Otherwise it goes to purchase
  price variance.
* **Issue to a run:** consumes layers. The run accumulates material cost.
* **Run completion:**
  * output unit cost = (material issued + labor) ÷ quantity completed;
  * labor = the outside shop's PO price, or in-house time × rate, or the run's labor estimate
    (flagged);
  * actual run costs feed `history` costing and in-house labor bids
    ([purchasing.md](purchasing.md) §6).

**Postings** (written to the outbox in the same transaction as the move:
[architecture.md](architecture.md) §6):

| Event | Posting (Dr / Cr) | Tagged with |
|---|---|---|
| Receipt from vendor | Inventory / GRNI (goods received, not invoiced) | PO |
| Issue to wip | WIP / Inventory | run |
| Run completion | Inventory / WIP | run |
| Outside-shop labor received | WIP / GRNI | run, PO |
| Shipment to customer | COGS / Inventory | order |
| Shipment to job | Jobs in process / Inventory | order |
| Job billed (job → customer) | COGS / Jobs in process | order |
| Adjustment or count | Inventory / Inventory variance (or the reverse) | — |
| Scrap | Scrap expense / Inventory (or WIP) | run or — |
| Transform | Inventory Y / Inventory X, with any variance | — |

Valuation classes map to Bonum accounts in a configuration table owned by operations, which
an accountant maintains. Planning states never post.

## 15. Roles

| Transition | Role |
|---|---|
| Create or edit quotes and orders; convert a quote | `sales` |
| Commit an order (creates demand); re-explode | `sales` with `approver`, or `sales_lead` |
| Create or commit POs and runs | `buyer` (normally through a round: [purchasing.md](purchasing.md)) |
| Release, issue, complete and close a run; record QC | `shop`, `shop_lead` (release, close); `qc` |
| Receive | `receiver` |
| Pick, pack, ship; returns | `shipper` |
| Transfer, adjust, count, transform | `inventory`; adjustments above a value threshold need `approver` |
| Reverse a done move | `inventory` + `approver` |
| Edit locations and valuation mapping | `admin` (mapping: `accountant`) |

## 16. ATI correspondence

| ATI | Here |
|---|---|
| `or` MTR in `work` | draft order or quote line, with no move |
| `or` in `open` / `clsd` | planned / done move from a committed order line |
| `po` | planned or done move from a PO line |
| `pt`, `wt` (round in progress) | purchasing round lines ([purchasing.md](purchasing.md)) |
| `wm` | run component move |
| `rq` | transfer (requisition from stock to a location) |
| `ad` | adjustment |
| `bf` | backflushed component move |
| automatic back-order | split of a partially executed move |
| `prd_part_inv` cache | maintained balances and planning views |
| projects 50 / 70 / 1 (hard-coded) | configurable locations and valuation classes |
